THE POSITION: Under the supervision of the Director, Region 4 Expanded Learning Programs, the Project Coordinator, Region 4 Expanded Learning Programs position supports regional initiatives designed to strengthen the quality and effectiveness of expanded learning programs. The Project Coordinator supports implementation of the Statewide System of Support for Expanded Learning (SSEL) approved Work Plan through professional learning, technical assistance, project coordination, and data management. Responsibilities include facilitating professional learning for frontline expanded learning staff, supporting Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) efforts, coordinating department-wide data systems, and maintaining regional data resources used to inform planning and service delivery. This position works collaboratively with local educational agencies (LEAs), community-based organizations, county offices of education, and the California Department of Education (CDE) to support expanded learning programs throughout Region 4. This position will be in person at ACOE, with some travel (approximately 15% time) to various locations throughout Region 4 and California.

LOCATION: 313 W. Winton Ave. Hayward, CA 94544

TYPICAL DUTIES: Collaborate with the Region 4 Expanded Learning Programs Department to support the implementation of county, regional, and statewide expanded learning initiatives. Design, coordinate, and facilitate professional learning opportunities, communities of practice, networking events, and other capacity-building activities for frontline expanded learning staff. Aggregate, organize, and maintain regional data files and datasets received from the California Department of Education (CDE) and other partners, ensuring data quality, consistency, accessibility, and timely updates. Co-coordinate and conduct in-person After School Education and Safety (ASES), 21st Century Community Learning Centers (21st CCLC), and Expanded Learning Opportunities Program (ELO-P) site visits, complete documentation, and coach frontline staff as needed to ensure program quality and compliance. Develop, adapt, and disseminate resources, tools, templates, and communications that support expanded learning programs. Maintain current knowledge of expanded learning legislation, policies, regulations, quality standards, and promising practices and disseminate information as appropriate. Friendly and detail-oriented project planner with a background in customer service and digital document management. A reliable team player dedicated to making a positive first impression.

Why CSUF

California State University, Fullerton (Cal State Fullerton) is a leading public university committed to student success, academic excellence, and inclusive excellence. The university fosters a collaborative environment that supports teaching, research, and service while promoting innovation and professional growth. Cal State Fullerton is both a Hispanic-Serving Institution and an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institution, and a recipient of the Seal of Excelencia (2021 and 2024) from Excelencia in Education. Joining Cal State Fullerton means becoming part of a community dedicated to advancing student achievement, career success, and economic mobility.

Department

The Pollak Library empowers and nurtures our academic community in the pursuit, discovery, and creation of knowledge. We strive to advance success of the academic community by providing access to an evolving collection, developing information literacy skills, creating innovative spaces, encouraging intellectual curiosity, and welcoming various perspectives. We seek an exceptional individual to join the Public Service department within the Division of Academic Affairs as the Exhibit Program Coordinator (Administrative Analyst/Specialist Exempt II). The ideal candidate in this role should have a positive attitude and an active, energetic mind characterized by highly ethical practices and a commitment to inclusivity, openness, flexibility, integrity, and kindness.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Exhibit Program Coordinator chairs the Exhibit Program Committee (composed of library faculty and staff) and serves as the primary contact for the program. Under general direction of the Dean of the Library and the Associate Dean of Public Services, the Exhibit Program Coordinator is responsible for exhibit program leadership, guidelines and procedures, and the determination of methods to meet goals and objectives with full accountability of results in a broad impact program. Works in consultation with the exhibit committee regarding exhibit programming and proposal review. Oversees day-to-day administration of the program, including occasional weeknights and weekends. The coordinator is responsible for hiring, training, and supervising student workers for projects related to the exhibit program. Assists with the library signage installation. Other duties as assigned.

Essential Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited four-year college or university and/or the equivalent training and administrative work experience involving the study, analysis, evaluation, development or improvement of administrative policies, procedures, practices, or programs plus four years of related experience. Working knowledge of and the ability to apply standard theories, principles, practices, and techniques applicable to the program and/or administrative specialty to develop conclusions and make recommendations. Thorough knowledge of the policies, procedures, and outside regulations pertaining to the applicable program and/or administrative specialty. Working knowledge of operational and fiscal analysis and techniques. Ability to take initiative and plan, organize, coordinate, and perform work in various situations where numerous and diverse demands are involved. Skilled in the research, development, and evaluation of policies and programs. Ability to collect, evaluate, and interpret data to develop sound conclusions and make appropriate recommendations. Expertise in investigating and analyzing problems with broad administrative impact and implications. Ability to anticipate problems, address them proactively, and develop appropriate recommendations leading to solutions. Demonstrated ability to effectively interpret, organize, and present information and ideas in written or presentation form and use consultative and facilitation skills to gain consensus. Ability to train others on new skills and procedures and provide lead work direction. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Access, and Outlook. Ability to communicate clearly and effectively both orally and in writing. Ability to establish and maintain effective and cooperative working relationships with others.

A background check (including a criminal records check) must be completed satisfactorily and is required for employment. CSU will make a conditional offer of employment, which may be rescinded if the background check reveals disqualifying information, and/or it is discovered that the candidate knowingly withheld or falsified information. Failure to complete the background check satisfactorily may affect the continued employment of a current CSU employee who was conditionally offered the position.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree from an accredited four-year college or university in museum science, anthropology, art history, or a related discipline and/or equivalent experience working in a related environment. Experience working in an academic setting.

jobs.title: Program Coordinator of Student Affairs - MEDEX Northwest
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Department of Family Medicine’s MEDEX Northwest Physician Assistant Program has an outstanding opportunity for a Program Coordinator (Student Affairs) to join their team.

About This Opportunity

Reporting to the Assistant Director of Student Services, the Program Coordinator (Student Affairs) provides operational management and project coordination for the MEDEX Student Affairs team. This position coordinates student support services, tutoring activities, Student Progress Committee operations, academic records, scheduling, and administrative projects supporting students and faculty across MEDEX Northwest’s multiple campuses.

The Program Coordinator serves as a primary resource for students, tutors, faculty, and staff navigating student support programs and related policies and procedures. The position exercises independent judgment when coordinating sensitive academic matters and maintains the confidentiality of student information in accordance with FERPA requirements and program accreditation standards.

Key Responsibilities

Student Affairs operations and student support coordination (30%): Manage day-to-day operations and projects for the Student Affairs team. Coordinate meetings among students, academic coaches, tutors, faculty, and staff; monitor student support activities; recommend strategies to improve outreach and scheduling; maintain operational procedures; and advise students, tutors, and faculty regarding student support processes and resources.
Tutoring program coordination (20%): Lead tutoring program logistics, including tutor outreach, onboarding, access to instructional resources, scheduling, attendance tracking, invoices, hours, and monthly payment documentation. Maintain tutor activity and student attendance records, monitor compliance with budgetary requirements, and initiate corrective action when needed.
Student Progress Committee support (20%): Coordinate regular and ad hoc Student Progress Committee meetings involving leadership, faculty, students, and other stakeholders. Prepare agendas, track student cases, collect relevant information, record confidential meeting minutes, distribute academic warning letters, communicate action items, and maintain committee files and records.
Academic records, Canvas, and administrative support (20%): Build and maintain Student Affairs courses in Canvas; track remediation and student support assignments; prepare completion reports; maintain student performance, accommodation, and disability-related absence records; draft, proofread, and edit correspondence; support presentations and virtual sessions; and organize records in accordance with retention requirements.
Scholarships, evaluation, and program initiatives (10%): Coordinate scholarship application and review logistics, advise students regarding scholarship requirements, compile application scores, and support award decisions. Collaborate on program evaluation activities and participate in accreditation, technology, orientation, graduation, retreat, and other program initiatives and events.

Required Qualifications

To be considered for this opportunity your application must demonstrate you meet both the minimum qualifications and additional qualifications listed below. Equivalent education and/or experience may substitute for minimum qualifications except when there are legal requirements, such as a license, certification, and/or registration.

Minimum Qualifications

Applicants who do not meet these qualifications WILL NOT be forwarded to the Hiring Manager.

High school graduation or equivalent AND two years of experience in the program specialty.
Equivalent education and/or experience may substitute for minimum qualifications except when there are legal requirements, such as a license, certification, and/or registration.

Additional Qualifications

Experience working with students experiencing academic difficulty, professionalism concerns, or other performance-related challenges.
Experience supporting student accommodations and collaborating with disability services offices.
Experience coordinating operations in a higher education, health professions education, or other accreditation-driven educational program.
Experience maintaining confidential student records under FERPA or comparable privacy requirements.
Experience supporting accreditation requirements related to student support, student progression, or program outcomes.
Experience supporting student remediation, tutoring, academic coaching, or other student-success initiatives.
Experience coordinating complex schedules involving students, faculty, staff, and multiple stakeholders.
Experience supporting academic committees through agenda preparation, meeting coordination, minute taking, case or action-item tracking, and follow-up.
Experience using Canvas or a comparable learning management system.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including developing and maintaining tracking databases and reporting tools.
Experience developing and maintaining operational procedures, workflow documentation, or filing and recordkeeping systems.
Demonstrated ability to communicate supportively and adapt communication to students with diverse experiences, learning needs, and communication styles.
Demonstrated discretion when handling sensitive academic, performance, professionalism, accommodation, or other confidential student matters.
Proficiency in drafting, proofreading, and editing professional correspondence.
Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, Outlook, and OneDrive, as well as database applications.
Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and complete projects accurately within established deadlines.
Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills when working with students, faculty, staff, and other stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting Physician Assistant, medical, nursing, or another health professions education program.
Experience coordinating student support services within an accredited health sciences program.
Experience supporting a student progress committee, academic review committee, or similar academic governance body.
Experience working with adult learners in graduate or professional education.
Experience working in a multi-campus or geographically distributed educational environment.

Working Conditions

Must learn the computer systems and software applications necessary to fulfill the position’s responsibilities, including Canvas, Catalyst, FileMaker Pro, PowerPoint, Zoom, and other applicable systems.
Must develop and maintain working knowledge of MEDEX policies and procedures necessary to provide operational coordination, project support, and guidance to students, tutors, faculty, and staff.
Must be available to participate in applicable administrative and academic meetings, projects, and events at the University of Washington campus in Seattle.
Must maintain confidentiality when working with protected student information and sensitive academic or professionalism matters.
Must occasionally carry lightweight office or classroom equipment.
Must be able to assist with in-person events, which may require walking some distance in inclement weather or driving a personal vehicle.

About The Team

MEDEX Northwest is the University of Washington’s Physician Assistant Program and a section of the Department of Family Medicine within the School of Medicine. MEDEX prepares physician assistants to serve communities throughout the region and operates across five campus locations: Anchorage, Alaska; Spokane, Washington; Kona, Hawaiʻi; Seattle, Washington; and Tacoma, Washington.

The Student Affairs team supports student success, academic progression, tutoring, coaching, accommodations, scholarships, and other services across the program. The Program Coordinator works collaboratively with Student Affairs leadership, faculty, academic coaches, tutors, students, and administrative colleagues throughout MEDEX’s multi-campus environment.

jobs.description:

Department: Office of Advancement

Job Title: Program Coordinator, Data Insights

Position #: 00741765 – Requisition #:
40608

Job Summary:

The Program Coordinator on the Philanthropic Growth and Data Insights team is a key contributor for the Office of Advancement at CU Anschutz. This position reports to the Managing Director of Development, Data Insights and will support reporting, analytics, technology roadmap, portfolio development, and data stewardship projects. Under minimal supervision, the Program Coordinator is responsible for creating, implementing and revising procedures around Data Insights project management and change management processes. The Program Coordinator will leverage knowledge of Advancement’s CU Ascend CRM and Advancement Intelligence reporting tool to support data entry and maintenance, ad hoc reporting and analysis, and identification of training for other team members in these resources. The Program Coordinator works closely with Data Insights staff, Advancement stakeholders, and campus and system partners to ensure projects are effectively planned, communicated, and implemented.

Supports administrative decision making and takes action in the manager’s absence, to include establishing project timelines and implementing with project management software, scheduling and adjusting project scopes and timelines as priorities shift, and supporting project management efforts. Additional duties are outlined below.

Supervision Received: Managing Director of Development, Data Insights
Supervision Exercised: No direct reports

Key Responsibilities:

Data Insights Project & Portfolio Management – 60%

Using project management tool (Asana), manage Data Insights project queue through request intake, requirements gathering, scope definition, tracking tool management, status updates communication, and project debriefs and documentation. Facilitates intake, triage and prioritization of project requests from Data Insights form submissions and team inbox.
Ensures projects and tasks are regularly updated and team members feel empowered to use the tool.
Schedules, creates agendas for, and leads project launch meetings as needed.
In partnership with Data Insights colleagues, communicates project scope and individual team member responsibilities to all stakeholders and captures items in Asana.
Takes detailed and clear notes during project meetings and disseminates information and assigned action items to the appropriate partners.
Technology roadmap and enhancement projects - attends cross-campus project meetings, often alongside Managing Director and other campus representatives, to ensure updates are captured, questions triaged and answered, and action items executed.
Portfolio development process - alongside Executive Strategist, Development Assistant and System Advancement liaisons, facilitates internal aspects of weekly referral and assignment process.
Ensures steps in process are executed and assignments are confirmed, documented and communicated in a timely fashion. Coordinates review from all parties involved, attends weekly meetings and supports follow-up action items.
System Advancement ticket reviews - participates in monthly Service Cloud ticket reviews with Managing Director and System Advancement Service Delivery team, to ensure campus colleagues’ requests are being properly communicated, prioritized and addressed.
Develops and maintains project management standards, templates, reports and documentation.

Change Management & Data Enablement – 25%

Supports change management by coordinating rollout and communications plans for new analytics, reporting and CRM initiatives (including user guides and how-to-videos), in partnership with Data Insights colleagues.
Gathers stakeholder feedback and identifies opportunities for continuous improvement.
Works with Managing Director to develop ongoing and episodic trainings for Advancement staff on use the of CRM and reporting tools.
Assists with data validation efforts on data insights reports and analysis.
Serves as an office Advancement Intelligence (AI) data expert, point-person and liaison for data use and compliance.

Administrative/Other Duties – 15%:

Performs own clerical and administrative tasks.
Assists Data Insights staff with data entry – including on referrals, contact reports, gift modifications, records merges, etc. in Salesforce and project updates in Asana - as needed
Utilizes data from Asana, Salesforce and reporting tools to generate requested reports, spreadsheets and correspondence on a routine basis.
In partnership with Data Insights colleagues and System Advancement, supports regular data hygiene audits and helps address data quality issues and inconsistencies.
Monitors team inbox in Outlook, along with Development Assistant, capturing and triaging new requests for projects, trainings or support.
Coordinates agendas for team meetings and monthly training sessions, in partnership with Managing Director and Executive Strategist.

Work Location:

Hybrid – this role is eligible for a hybrid schedule of 3 days per week on campus and as needed for in-person meetings.

Why Join Us:

Philanthropy brings people together; it’s a driving force in accelerating the pace of discovery, attracting and retaining excellent students and faculty, and delivering world-class prevention and care.

At the Office of Advancement at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, we put our passions to work.

We have the privilege to collaborate with people who want to make a difference in the world – people who want to make an impact on humanity that may be felt long after they have passed. Our office exists to ensure stakeholders within and outside the university know, value, and support the important work being done on this academic medical campus.

We have AMAZING benefits and offer exceptional amounts of holiday, vacation and sick leave! The University of Colorado offers an excellent benefits package including:

Medical: Multiple plan options
Dental: Multiple plan options
Additional Insurance: Disability, Life, Vision

ECO Pass: Reduced rate RTD Bus and light rail service

There are many additional perks & programs with the CU Advantage.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.
Substitution: A combination of education and related technical/military/paraprofessional experience may be substituted for a bachelor’s degree on a year for year basis.

1 years of professional development, business administration, project management or data analysis experience.

Applicants must meet minimum qualifications at the time of hire.

Preferred Qualifications:

At least 3 years of professional related work experience.
Professional experience working in nonprofit development/fundraising, higher education or health care, with at least 1 year of project management experience.
Experience using project management software, such as Asana, Monday or a similar tool.
Experience working with donor CRM or database software, such as Salesforce or a similar tool.
Experience using reporting and analytics tools, such as Tableau, Power BI or IBM Cognos.
Experience with and knowledge of HIPAA rules and regulations

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship. We are unable to provide work visa sponsorship or employment authorization for this position now or in the future.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Ability to communicate effectively, both in writing and orally, to keep stakeholders informed and projects on track.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees at all levels throughout the institution.
Outstanding customer service skills.
Attention to detail.

jobs.title: GIS Analyst III
jobs.description:
Primary Talent Partners has a new contract opening for a GIS Analyst III
with our large power and utilities client. This is a 3-year contract with a potential for extension. 

This is a remote opportunity with a preference for candidates located in either North or South Carolina.

Pay:
$32.50 - $37.50/hr
; W2 contract, no PTO, no Benefits. ACA-compliant supplemental package available for enrollment.

Description:
The GIS Analyst for Transmission Vegetation Management is a highly specialized role that provides essential geospatial and analytical support to ***’s Transmission Vegetation Management operations.
This position is integral to ensuring safe, reliable, and cost-effective delivery of electric power by enabling informed decision-making through advanced data analysis and geospatial technologies.
The GIS Analyst is responsible for pulling and analyzing GIS data to define the scope of work for field operations, performing complex spatial analyses to deliver actionable insights, and maintaining the integrity of geospatial datasets through rigorous updates and adherence to established data standards. By ensuring accuracy and consistency in data, the analyst safeguards the reliability of work execution systems that operational teams depend on for planning and compliance.

In addition to core responsibilities, the GIS Analyst provides technical expertise in querying and reporting data using SQL and is expected to perform ad-hoc analysis to address evolving business needs. A strong preference is given to candidates who can leverage Python for workflow automation, enabling process efficiencies and reducing manual effort.
Proficiency in industry-standard tools such as ArcGIS, ArcMap, and geoprocessing technologies is essential, along with the ability to integrate data visualization techniques to communicate insights effectively.
The role demands a high level of problem-solving capability, attention to detail, and adaptability to support dynamic operational requirements.

Collaboration and communication are critical components of this position. The GIS Analyst works closely with internal teams and external stakeholders, providing responsive support and resolving issues that impact operational performance.
This includes interpreting complex datasets, troubleshooting data discrepancies, and ensuring that end users can fully utilize work execution systems. While knowledge of vegetation management practices within the utility sector is advantageous, it is not mandatory; however, the ability to quickly understand operational workflows and align geospatial solutions to business objectives is key.
Beyond technical execution, the GIS Analyst contributes to continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to enhance data processes, streamline reporting, and implement best practices across the team.
The role supports ***’s commitment to compliance with regulatory standards and plays a pivotal part in optimizing vegetation management strategies that protect infrastructure and maintain service reliability.
By combining advanced technical skills with a strong customer service orientation, the GIS Analyst ensures that data-driven solutions translate into operational success, reinforcing ***’s mission to deliver safe, reliable, and efficient electric service.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, gender identity, or any other factor protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

About RohmTek

RohmTek is a science-first provider of advanced geochemical laboratory services and portable analytical instrumentation. Serving clients across the energy, environmental, and industrial sectors, our team specializes in high-resolution data acquisition and interpretation using handheld XRF, XRD, and other field-deployable analytical platforms.

Position Overview

The Field Project Coordinator supports RohmTek's 24/7 field operations by performing geochemical data QA/QC and preparing timely, accurate reports for active wellsite projects. The primary responsibility of this position is to provide weekend reporting coverage, ensuring continuity between weekday and weekend operations and meeting established client reporting deadlines.
This entry to intermediate level position, and serves as an important connection between field personnel, RohmTek's internal operations team, and clients. The analyst reviews incoming geochemical data, identifies potential data-quality issues, applies standardized calibration and normalization workflows, prepares client deliverables, and communicates significant findings or operational concerns to the appropriate team members.
The position may also assist with instrument logistics, field-user troubleshooting, and process improvements when reporting responsibilities and project demands allow.

Key Responsibilities

Weekend Reporting and QA/QC

Provide primary QA/QC and reporting coverage for active wellsite projects during scheduled weekend hours.
Review incoming wellsite geochemical datasets, predominantly handheld XRF data, for completeness, consistency, and analytical quality.
Prepare, review, and deliver client reports according to established weekend reporting schedules and deadlines.
Calibrate, validate, and normalize XRF data using RohmTek's standardized workflows and applicable client-specific requirements.
Identify missing, inconsistent, or anomalous data and coordinate with field personnel to resolve issues before report delivery.
Generate preliminary geochemical interpretations, including elemental trends, mineral indicators, and observations related to drill cuttings.
Confirm that report formats, project information, naming conventions, and supporting documentation are accurate and consistent.
Maintain clear handoff documentation between weekday and weekend team members.
Escalate significant data-quality, instrument, or reporting issues to the Field Operations Manager or appropriate technical personnel.
Maintain accurate records of completed reports, report revisions, client communications, and unresolved project issues.

Field and Client Support

Provide technical support and troubleshooting guidance to field users.
Help ensure consistent sample analysis, data collection, and reporting practices across active projects.
Respond professionally and promptly to reporting questions and time-sensitive operational requests.
Support RohmTek's 24/7 field service model through scheduled weekend and rotational coverage, with no overnight shifts.

Qualifications

Experience in geoscience, mudlogging, wellsite services, or a related technical field.
Strong working knowledge of XRF (elemental) data and geochemical QA/QC practices.
Ability and willingness to work a weekend-focused schedule and meet time-sensitive reporting deadlines.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office, including pivot tables, lookups, data formatting, and basic charts.
Experience with StarSteer or another geosteering platform is preferred but not required.
Strong organizational, written communication, and client-service skills.
Ability to review technical data carefully and recognize potential analytical or operational problems.
Experience working in a laboratory environment is a plus.
Bachelor's degree in geology, geochemistry, earth sciences, or a related field is preferred.

Ideal Candidate Traits

Dependable and comfortable taking ownership of weekend reporting responsibilities.
Detail-oriented and committed to accurate, consistent client deliverables.
Proactive and process-driven.
Comfortable managing multiple active projects and competing deadlines.
Able to work independently while maintaining clear communication with the broader operations team.

jobs.title: What Does a Data Analyst Do? Your 2026 Career Guide
jobs.description:
Key takeaways

About

Data analysts collect, clean, and interpret data sets to solve problems, answer questions, and identify insights for employers. At a glance, here's what you need to know about this impactful career:

Data analysts earn competitive pay. According to Glassdoor, the median total pay for data analysts is $93,000 a year as of March 2026 [1].
In there jobs, data analysts answer questions like: What kind of customers should a business target in its next ad campaign? What age group is most vulnerable to a particular disease? What patterns in behavior are connected to financial fraud?
They work in many industries, including business, finance, criminal justice, science, medicine, and government.

In this article, we'll discuss more about what data analysts do, what skills you'll need to pursue this career, and how you can start on a path to becoming one. Afterward, if you want to start working toward a data career by building job-relevant skills and earning a respected credential, consider enrolling in the Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate.

What is data analysis?

Data Analysis Is The Process Of Gleaning Insights From Data To Inform Better Business Decisions. The Process Of Analyzing Data Typically Moves Through Five Iterative Phases

Identify the data you want to analyze
Collect the data
Clean the data in preparation for analysis
Analyze the data
Interpret the results of the analysis

Data analysis can take different forms, depending on the question you’re trying to answer. Descriptive analysis tells us what happened; diagnostic analysis tells us why it happened; predictive analytics forms projections about the future; and, finally, prescriptive analysis creates actionable advice on what actions to take.

What does a data analyst do?

A data analyst gathers and interprets data in order to solve a specific problem. The role involves plenty of time spent with data but also entails communicating findings to stakeholders.

Here’s what many data analysts do on a day-to-day basis:

Gather data: Analysts often collect data themselves. This could include conducting surveys, tracking visitor characteristics on a company website, or buying datasets from data collection specialists.
Clean data: Raw data might contain duplicates, errors, or outliers. Cleaning the data means maintaining the quality of data in a spreadsheet or through a programming language so that your interpretations won’t be wrong or skewed.
Model data: This entails creating and designing the structures of a database. You might choose what types of data to store and collect, establish how data categories are related to each other, and work through how the data actually appears.
Interpret data: Interpreting data involves finding patterns or trends in data that could answer the question at hand.
Present: Communicating the results of your findings will be a key part of your job. You do this by putting together visualizations like charts and graphs, writing reports, and presenting information to interested parties.

What tools do data analysts use?

During The Process Of Data Analysis, Analysts Often Use a Wide Variety Of Tools To Make Their Work More Accurate And Efficient. Some Of The Most Common Tools In The Data Analytics Industry Include

Microsoft Excel
Google Sheets
SQL
Tableau
R or Python
SAS
Microsoft Power BI
Jupyter Notebooks

Learn how to perform data analysis, including data preparation, statistical analysis, and predictive modeling using R, R Studio, and Jupyter in the IBM Data Analytics with Excel and R Professional Certificate.

How much do data analysts make? Data analyst salary and job outlook

Data analysts earn a median total pay of $93,000 a year, according to Glassdoor [1]. This includes base pay and additional compensation but the exact amount can vary depending on your seniority, where in the US you’re located, and other factors.

Data analysts are in high demand. The World Economic Forum listed them as one of the fastest-growing jobs between 2025 and 2030 [2]. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) also reports that related occupations have high growth rates. From 2024 to 2034, operations research analyst positions are expected to grow by 21 percent, data scientists by 34 percent, market research analysts by 7 percent, and mathematicians and statisticians by 8 percent. That’s a lot higher than the total employment growth rate of just 3 percent over the decade.

Data analyst vs. data scientist: What’s the difference?

Data analysts and data scientists both work with data, but what they do with it differs. Data analysts typically work with existing data to solve defined business problems. Data scientists build new algorithms and models to make predictions about the future. Learn more about the difference between data scientists and data analysts.

Types of data analysts

As advancing technology has rapidly expanded the types and amount of information we can collect, knowing how to gather, sort, and analyze data has become a crucial part of almost any industry. You’ll find data analysts in the criminal justice, fashion, food, technology, business, environment, and public sectors—among many others.

People who perform data analysis might have other titles, such as:

Medical and health care analyst
Market research analyst
Business analyst
Business intelligence analyst
Operations research analyst
Intelligence analyst

Interested in business intelligence?

Gain the business and data skills you need for an entry-level business analyst role with IBM's Business Analyst Professional Certificate program. In as little as three months, you'll gain critical skills like business systems analysis, project risk management, and interactive data visualization.

How to become a data analyst

You can find data analytics jobs in all sorts of industries, and there’s more than one path toward securing your first job in this high-demand field. Whether you’re just getting started in the professional world or pivoting to a new career, here are some steps toward becoming a data analyst.

Get a foundational education.

If you’re new to the world of data analysis, you’ll want to start by developing some foundational knowledge in the field. Getting a broad overview of data analytics can help you decide whether this career is a good fit while equipping you with job-ready skills.

It used to be that most entry-level data analyst positions required a bachelor’s degree. While many positions still do require a degree, that’s beginning to change. You can develop foundational knowledge and enhance your resume with a degree in math, computer science, or another related field— or you can also learn what you need through alternative programs, like professional certificates, bootcamps, or self-study courses.

Resources to start your data analyst career

We've curated a collection of resources to help you decide whether becoming a data analyst is right for you—including figuring out what skills you'll need to learn and courses you can take to pursue this career.

Build your technical skills.

Getting a job in data analysis typically requires having a set of specific technical skills. Whether you’re learning through a degree program, professional certificate, or on your own, these are some essential skills you’ll likely need to get hired.

Statistics
R or Python programming
SQL (Structured Query Language)
Data visualization
Data cleaning and preparation

Take a look at some job listings for roles you’d like to apply for, and focus your learning on the specific programming languages or visualization tools listed as requirements.

In addition to these hard skills, hiring managers also look for workplace skills, like solid communication skills—you may be asked to present your findings to those without as much technical knowledge—problem-solving ability, and domain knowledge in the industry you’d like to work.

Learn more:
7 In-Demand Data Analyst Skills to Get Hired

Work on projects with real data.

The best way to learn how to find value in data is to work with it in real-world settings. Look for degree programs or courses that include hands-on projects using real data sets. You can also find a variety of free public data sets you can use to design your own projects.

Dig into climate data from the National Centers for Environmental Information, delve deeper into the news with data from BuzzFeed, or come up with solutions to looming challenges on Earth and beyond with NASA open data. These are just a few examples of the data out there. Pick a topic you’re interested in and find some data to practice on.

Read more:
5 Data Analytics Projects for Beginners

Develop a portfolio of your work.

As you play around with data sets on the internet or complete hands-on assignments in your classes, be sure to save your best work for your portfolio. A portfolio demonstrates your skills to hiring managers. A strong portfolio can go a long way toward getting the job.

As you start to curate work for your portfolio, choose projects that demonstrate your ability to:

Scrape data from different sources
Clean and normalize raw data
Visualize your findings through graphs, charts, maps, and other visualizations
Draw actionable insights from data

If you’ve worked on any group projects through the course of your learning, consider including one of those as well. This shows that you’re able to work as part of a team.

If you’re not sure what to include in your portfolio (or need some inspiration for project ideas), spend some time browsing through other people’s portfolios to see what they’ve chosen to include.

Read more:
How to Build a Data Analyst Portfolio: Tips for Success

Get an entry-level data analyst job.

After gaining some experience working with data and presenting your findings, it’s time to polish your resume and begin applying for entry-level data analyst jobs. Don’t be afraid to apply for positions that feel like a stretch. Your skills, portfolio, and enthusiasm for a role can often matter more than if you check every bullet item in the qualifications list.

If you’re still in school, ask your university’s career services office about any internship opportunities. With an internship, you can start gaining real-world experience for your resume and apply what you’re learning on the job.

There’s more than one path toward a career as a data analyst. Whether you've just graduated from school or are looking to switch careers, the first step is often assessing what transferable skills you have and building the new skills you’ll need in this new role.

Consider certification or an advanced degree.

As you move through your career as a data analyst, consider how you’d like to advance and what other qualifications can help you get there. Certifications, like the Certified Analytics Professional or Cloudera Certified Associate Data Analyst, may help qualify you for more advanced positions at higher pay grades.

If you’re considering advancing into a role as a data scientist, you may need to earn a master’s degree in data science or a related field. Advanced degrees are not always required, but having one can open up more opportunities.

Data analyst career advancement

Being a data analyst can also open doors to other careers. Many who start as data analysts go on to work as data scientists. Like analysts, data scientists use statistics, math, and computer science to analyze data. A scientist, however, might use advanced techniques to build models and other tools to provide insights into future trends. Further your data analytics career with the Google Advanced Data Analytics Professional Certificate.

Build your data analyst skills today

Skills

Data analysts use their knowledge to help others make more informed decisions. Build the skills you need for this in-demand and fast-growing career with these resources from Coursera:

Watch on YouTube: Careers You Can Pursue with a Data Analytics Degree

Perform additional duties as assigned to support company initiatives and project success.

3+ years of field-based experience in materials testing, construction inspection, geotechnical fieldwork, or a related industry.
Industry certifications such as ACI Level 1 Concrete Testing preferred or ability to obtain within a specified time period.
Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record; ability to safely operate company vehicles.
Commitment to safety and adherence to OSHA regulations, industry best practices, and company safety policies.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) and Field Data Collection (FDC) software or similar industry tools.
Mathematical skills sufficient to add, subtract, multiply, and divide into all units of measure using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals.
Ability to read, write, and interpret blueprints, procedures, manuals, technical documents, and reports related to drilling, safety, and project requirements.
Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment.
Strong time management, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to complete tasks efficiently and accurately.

Adherence to all company safety protocols and use of PPE is required during travel and on-site work.

#LD-MD1

Physical Demands & Work Environment

This position primarily works in an outdoor work environment, regularly exposed to varying field conditions, including:

Sites that may not be accessible by vehicle, requiring travel on foot through wetlands, swamps, grasslands, fields, and other uneven or rugged terrain with natural and man-made obstacles such as sand, brush, and debris.
Moderate to loud noise levels, common in active construction and industrial environments.
Exposure to environmental elements including dirt, dust, sun, heat, humidity, and adverse weather conditions.

Ability to lift and/or carry 35 to 50 lbs. up to 75 feet, involving regular repetitive motion.

Query and analyze large datasets to extract and communicate meaningful insights

Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Looker, Omni, Sigma)

A collaborative team player who thrives on a small analytics team
You love teaching almost as much as you love a clean dataset - nothing makes you happier than watching a teammate go from confused to confident

Experience with dbt or modern data stack tools is a plus

We love our staff, and show it with benefits (including but not limited to medical, dental, vision, FSA, and life insurance), matching retirement plan, generous and flexible paid time off, Purple Carrot box delivery credits, professional development, and the opportunity to work in collaboration with teammates who are passionate about food!

University of Colorado Anschutz

Department: Office of Advancement

Job Title: Program Coordinator, Data Insights

Position #: 00741765 – Requisition #:
40608

Job Summary:

The Program Coordinator on the Philanthropic Growth and Data Insights team is a key contributor for the Office of Advancement at CU Anschutz. This position reports to the Managing Director of Development, Data Insights and will support reporting, analytics, technology roadmap, portfolio development, and data stewardship projects. Under minimal supervision, the Program Coordinator is responsible for creating, implementing and revising procedures around Data Insights project management and change management processes. The Program Coordinator will leverage knowledge of Advancement’s CU Ascend CRM and Advancement Intelligence reporting tool to support data entry and maintenance, ad hoc reporting and analysis, and identification of training for other team members in these resources. The Program Coordinator works closely with Data Insights staff, Advancement stakeholders, and campus and system partners to ensure projects are effectively planned, communicated, and implemented.

Supports administrative decision making and takes action in the manager’s absence, to include establishing project timelines and implementing with project management software, scheduling and adjusting project scopes and timelines as priorities shift, and supporting project management efforts. Additional duties are outlined below.

Supervision Received: Managing Director of Development, Data Insights
Supervision Exercised: No direct reports

Key Responsibilities:

Data Insights Project & Portfolio Management – 60%

Using project management tool (Asana), manage Data Insights project queue through request intake, requirements gathering, scope definition, tracking tool management, status updates communication, and project debriefs and documentation. Facilitates intake, triage and prioritization of project requests from Data Insights form submissions and team inbox.
Ensures projects and tasks are regularly updated and team members feel empowered to use the tool.
Schedules, creates agendas for, and leads project launch meetings as needed.
In partnership with Data Insights colleagues, communicates project scope and individual team member responsibilities to all stakeholders and captures items in Asana.
Takes detailed and clear notes during project meetings and disseminates information and assigned action items to the appropriate partners.
Technology roadmap and enhancement projects - attends cross-campus project meetings, often alongside Managing Director and other campus representatives, to ensure updates are captured, questions triaged and answered, and action items executed.
Portfolio development process - alongside Executive Strategist, Development Assistant and System Advancement liaisons, facilitates internal aspects of weekly referral and assignment process.
Ensures steps in process are executed and assignments are confirmed, documented and communicated in a timely fashion. Coordinates review from all parties involved, attends weekly meetings and supports follow-up action items.
System Advancement ticket reviews - participates in monthly Service Cloud ticket reviews with Managing Director and System Advancement Service Delivery team, to ensure campus colleagues’ requests are being properly communicated, prioritized and addressed.
Develops and maintains project management standards, templates, reports and documentation.

Change Management & Data Enablement – 25%

Supports change management by coordinating rollout and communications plans for new analytics, reporting and CRM initiatives (including user guides and how-to-videos), in partnership with Data Insights colleagues.
Gathers stakeholder feedback and identifies opportunities for continuous improvement.
Works with Managing Director to develop ongoing and episodic trainings for Advancement staff on use the of CRM and reporting tools.
Assists with data validation efforts on data insights reports and analysis.
Serves as an office Advancement Intelligence (AI) data expert, point-person and liaison for data use and compliance.

Administrative/Other Duties – 15%:

Performs own clerical and administrative tasks.
Assists Data Insights staff with data entry – including on referrals, contact reports, gift modifications, records merges, etc. in Salesforce and project updates in Asana - as needed
Utilizes data from Asana, Salesforce and reporting tools to generate requested reports, spreadsheets and correspondence on a routine basis.
In partnership with Data Insights colleagues and System Advancement, supports regular data hygiene audits and helps address data quality issues and inconsistencies.
Monitors team inbox in Outlook, along with Development Assistant, capturing and triaging new requests for projects, trainings or support.
Coordinates agendas for team meetings and monthly training sessions, in partnership with Managing Director and Executive Strategist.

Work Location:

Hybrid – this role is eligible for a hybrid schedule of 3 days per week on campus and as needed for in-person meetings.

Why Join Us:

Philanthropy brings people together; it’s a driving force in accelerating the pace of discovery, attracting and retaining excellent students and faculty, and delivering world-class prevention and care.

At the Office of Advancement at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, we put our passions to work.

We have the privilege to collaborate with people who want to make a difference in the world – people who want to make an impact on humanity that may be felt long after they have passed. Our office exists to ensure stakeholders within and outside the university know, value, and support the important work being done on this academic medical campus.

Why work for the University?

We have AMAZING benefits and offer exceptional amounts of holiday, vacation and sick leave! The University of Colorado offers an excellent benefits package including:

Medical: Multiple plan options
Dental: Multiple plan options
Additional Insurance: Disability, Life, Vision
Retirement 401(a) Plan: Employer contributes 10% of your gross pay
Paid Time Off: Accruals over the year
Vacation Days: 22/year (maximum accrual 352 hours)
Sick Days: 15/year (unlimited maximum accrual)
Holiday Days: 15/year
Tuition Benefit: Employees have access to this benefit on all CU campuses
ECO Pass: Reduced rate RTD Bus and light rail service

There are many additional perks & programs with the CU Advantage.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.
Substitution: A combination of education and related technical/military/paraprofessional experience may be substituted for a bachelor’s degree on a year for year basis.

1 years of professional development, business administration, project management or data analysis experience.

Applicants must meet minimum qualifications at the time of hire.

Preferred Qualifications:

At least 3 years of professional related work experience.
Professional experience working in nonprofit development/fundraising, higher education or health care, with at least 1 year of project management experience.
Experience using project management software, such as Asana, Monday or a similar tool.
Experience working with donor CRM or database software, such as Salesforce or a similar tool.
Experience using reporting and analytics tools, such as Tableau, Power BI or IBM Cognos.
Experience with and knowledge of HIPAA rules and regulations

Conditions of Employment:

May be asked to work after hours and/or weekends for benefactor-related functions periodically.
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship. We are unable to provide work visa sponsorship or employment authorization for this position now or in the future.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Key skills include time management, a flexible and solutions-oriented mindset, strong organization skills, and an interest in partnering with many different colleagues on meaningful initiatives.
Ability to communicate effectively, both in writing and orally, to keep stakeholders informed and projects on track.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees at all levels throughout the institution.
Outstanding customer service skills.
Attention to detail.
Expert knowledge of Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
Solid knowledge of fundraising concepts, preferably in a higher education setting and/or healthcare non-profit
Demonstrated commitment and ability to advance diversity and inclusion.
Ability to lead through influence versus authority.

A letter of interest describing relevant job experiences as they relate to listed job qualifications and interest in the position
Curriculum vitae / Resume
Three to five professional references, including name, address, phone number (mobile number if appropriate), and email address

Questions should be directed to: Shannon Palombi, Shannon.Palombi@cuanschutz.edu

Applications will be accepted until finalists are identified, but preference will be given to complete applications received by August 5, 2026.
Those who do not apply by this date may or may not be considered.

Summary

Job Summary

CTWI’s Advising for Future-Ready Students program encourages applications for a temporary project coordinator! Our program prepares counselors, educators, and others in student advising roles to support students in navigating technology across educational, career, and social/emotional domains. By sharing information and support, students are better positioned to explore how technology intersects with their passions to open a world of opportunities.

CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

Who We Are

CTWI is a thriving community of more than 1,500 change leader organizations spanning K-12, Higher Education, and Industry that works to widen participation in technology fields and careers through innovative programs and research. CTWI helps organizations remain globally competitive in science and technology by creating environments where all students and employees thrive.

The CTWI organization is part of the College of Engineering & Applied Science at the University of Colorado-Boulder. It spans both university staffing, financial and legal procedures, and in addition, receives funding from a non-profit 501(c)(3), to implement financial, legal, and governance procedures on its behalf.

Responsibilities

What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be

The Advising for Future-Ready Students Project Coordinator will plan and coordinate projects including workshops, webinars, conferences and other engagements, to ensure they are completed in a timely fashion and meet project goals. Specific activities include:

Coordinate and lead numerous projects including workshops, webinars, conferences and other engagements using the organization's project management system.
Contribute to the maintenance of the program database, website, tracking systems, and records.
Set and negotiate deadlines, and prioritize tasks within and between multiple projects.
Coordinate tasks on projects with the Future-Ready team as consistent with their roles/responsibilities.
Serve as a point of contact for the Future-Ready team when multiple individuals are assigned to the same project to ensure team actions remain collaborative.

Identify and communicate potential barriers to project completion and outline potential solutions.
Adjust schedules and targets on projects as needed or financing for the project change.
Prepare weekly project status reports by capturing, analyzing, and summarizing relevant information.
Measure project performance (total time spent on project, percentage of tasks completed on time, achievement delivery, etc.) to identify areas for improvement.
Coordinate the development of project management manuals, training materials, and other documents to enable successful implementation and turnover of the process or system to others.
Monitor and maintain Future-Ready’s customer service and helpdesk systems.
Prepare weekly agenda items for team meetings- including tasks that are essential, overdue, and due within the next 5-7 business days to discuss as needed.
Attend weekly virtual meetings and as requested by the Future-Ready Team.
Other activities and tasks as assigned.

What You Should Know

This is a remote, temporary position working approximately 30 hours per week.

The hire rate for this position will be $28.00 - $35.00 per hour.

Benefits

Temporary positions at the University of Colorado are not benefits-eligible, however, all positions are eligible for paid sick leave .

Be resourceful. Be collaborative. Be Boulder.

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with one year or more of related professional experience. Equivalent combination of experience and education may substitute.

What You Will Need

Detail oriented with excellent project management skills.
Ability to multitask, change priorities as needed and follow through with all assignments.
Agile attitude.
Strong communication and time management skills.
Ability to delegate tasks effectively.
Ability to solve problems creatively.
Experience seeing projects through the full life cycle.
Demonstrated ability to work both autonomously and collaboratively.

What We Would Like You To Have

Working knowledge and experience with Project Management software and databases
Project Management Certification or relevant experience
Experience with Wrike and Airtable management systems
Experience in nonprofit mission driven organization

Special Instructions

To Apply, Please Submit The Following Materials

A current resume.
A cover letter that specifically tells us how your background and experience align with the requirements, qualifications, and responsibilities of the position.

We may request references at a later time.

Please apply by July 28, 2026
for consideration.

Note: Application materials will not be accepted via email. For consideration, please apply through CU Boulder Jobs .

new_jobs.title: GIS Analyst III
new_jobs.description:
Primary Talent Partners has a new contract opening for a GIS Analyst III
with our large power and utilities client. This is a 3-year contract with a potential for extension. 

This is a remote opportunity with a preference for candidates located in either North or South Carolina.

Pay:
$32.50 - $37.50/hr
; W2 contract, no PTO, no Benefits. ACA-compliant supplemental package available for enrollment.

Description:
The GIS Analyst for Transmission Vegetation Management is a highly specialized role that provides essential geospatial and analytical support to ***’s Transmission Vegetation Management operations.
This position is integral to ensuring safe, reliable, and cost-effective delivery of electric power by enabling informed decision-making through advanced data analysis and geospatial technologies.
The GIS Analyst is responsible for pulling and analyzing GIS data to define the scope of work for field operations, performing complex spatial analyses to deliver actionable insights, and maintaining the integrity of geospatial datasets through rigorous updates and adherence to established data standards. By ensuring accuracy and consistency in data, the analyst safeguards the reliability of work execution systems that operational teams depend on for planning and compliance.

In addition to core responsibilities, the GIS Analyst provides technical expertise in querying and reporting data using SQL and is expected to perform ad-hoc analysis to address evolving business needs. A strong preference is given to candidates who can leverage Python for workflow automation, enabling process efficiencies and reducing manual effort.
Proficiency in industry-standard tools such as ArcGIS, ArcMap, and geoprocessing technologies is essential, along with the ability to integrate data visualization techniques to communicate insights effectively.
The role demands a high level of problem-solving capability, attention to detail, and adaptability to support dynamic operational requirements.

Collaboration and communication are critical components of this position. The GIS Analyst works closely with internal teams and external stakeholders, providing responsive support and resolving issues that impact operational performance.
This includes interpreting complex datasets, troubleshooting data discrepancies, and ensuring that end users can fully utilize work execution systems. While knowledge of vegetation management practices within the utility sector is advantageous, it is not mandatory; however, the ability to quickly understand operational workflows and align geospatial solutions to business objectives is key.
Beyond technical execution, the GIS Analyst contributes to continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to enhance data processes, streamline reporting, and implement best practices across the team.
The role supports ***’s commitment to compliance with regulatory standards and plays a pivotal part in optimizing vegetation management strategies that protect infrastructure and maintain service reliability.
By combining advanced technical skills with a strong customer service orientation, the GIS Analyst ensures that data-driven solutions translate into operational success, reinforcing ***’s mission to deliver safe, reliable, and efficient electric service.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, gender identity, or any other factor protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

new_jobs.title: Hydrogeologist Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Project Manager- Hydrogeologist - Bozeman, MT

AE2S is seeking a Project Manager - Hydrogeologist in Bozeman, MT who will play a key role in project delivery and business development to support our western Montana operations. The ideal individual will have the opportunity to collaborate in developing, planning, designing, and implementing groundwater resource management solutions.

Responsibilities

Perform a variety of roles within project delivery (project management, QA/QC, and performing) related to groundwater and water resources engineering.
Grow market and technical presence within the region, prioritize client pursuits, build client relationships, provide client management, identify opportunities, and support proposal pursuits. Conduct groundwater resource evaluations.
Coordinate well permitting, drilling, design, construction, testing, sampling, rehabilitation and/or abandonment.
Develop, design, calibrate, and interpret groundwater flow and predictive modeling results.
Develop hydrogeologic models, groundwater sustainability plans, water supply assessments and strategies.
Manage multi-disciplinary resources to deliver high quality projects that meet or exceed clients' expectations.
Analyze data using a variety of techniques such as GIS, geo-statistics, statistics, or time-series analysis.
Analyze aquifer pumping test data and interpret borehole geophysical data; apply interpretation results to project and assess potential impacts of groundwater withdrawals on nearby users and the resource.

new_jobs.title: What Does a Data Analyst Do? Your 2026 Career Guide
new_jobs.description:
Key takeaways

About

Data analysts collect, clean, and interpret data sets to solve problems, answer questions, and identify insights for employers. At a glance, here's what you need to know about this impactful career:

Data analysts earn competitive pay. According to Glassdoor, the median total pay for data analysts is $93,000 a year as of March 2026 [1].
In there jobs, data analysts answer questions like: What kind of customers should a business target in its next ad campaign? What age group is most vulnerable to a particular disease? What patterns in behavior are connected to financial fraud?
They work in many industries, including business, finance, criminal justice, science, medicine, and government.

In this article, we'll discuss more about what data analysts do, what skills you'll need to pursue this career, and how you can start on a path to becoming one. Afterward, if you want to start working toward a data career by building job-relevant skills and earning a respected credential, consider enrolling in the Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate.

What is data analysis?

Data Analysis Is The Process Of Gleaning Insights From Data To Inform Better Business Decisions. The Process Of Analyzing Data Typically Moves Through Five Iterative Phases

Identify the data you want to analyze
Collect the data
Clean the data in preparation for analysis
Analyze the data
Interpret the results of the analysis

Data analysis can take different forms, depending on the question you’re trying to answer. Descriptive analysis tells us what happened; diagnostic analysis tells us why it happened; predictive analytics forms projections about the future; and, finally, prescriptive analysis creates actionable advice on what actions to take.

What does a data analyst do?

A data analyst gathers and interprets data in order to solve a specific problem. The role involves plenty of time spent with data but also entails communicating findings to stakeholders.

Here’s what many data analysts do on a day-to-day basis:

Gather data: Analysts often collect data themselves. This could include conducting surveys, tracking visitor characteristics on a company website, or buying datasets from data collection specialists.
Clean data: Raw data might contain duplicates, errors, or outliers. Cleaning the data means maintaining the quality of data in a spreadsheet or through a programming language so that your interpretations won’t be wrong or skewed.
Model data: This entails creating and designing the structures of a database. You might choose what types of data to store and collect, establish how data categories are related to each other, and work through how the data actually appears.
Interpret data: Interpreting data involves finding patterns or trends in data that could answer the question at hand.
Present: Communicating the results of your findings will be a key part of your job. You do this by putting together visualizations like charts and graphs, writing reports, and presenting information to interested parties.

What tools do data analysts use?

During The Process Of Data Analysis, Analysts Often Use a Wide Variety Of Tools To Make Their Work More Accurate And Efficient. Some Of The Most Common Tools In The Data Analytics Industry Include

Microsoft Excel
Google Sheets
SQL
Tableau
R or Python
SAS
Microsoft Power BI
Jupyter Notebooks

Learn how to perform data analysis, including data preparation, statistical analysis, and predictive modeling using R, R Studio, and Jupyter in the IBM Data Analytics with Excel and R Professional Certificate.

How much do data analysts make? Data analyst salary and job outlook

Data analysts earn a median total pay of $93,000 a year, according to Glassdoor [1]. This includes base pay and additional compensation but the exact amount can vary depending on your seniority, where in the US you’re located, and other factors.

Data analysts are in high demand. The World Economic Forum listed them as one of the fastest-growing jobs between 2025 and 2030 [2]. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) also reports that related occupations have high growth rates. From 2024 to 2034, operations research analyst positions are expected to grow by 21 percent, data scientists by 34 percent, market research analysts by 7 percent, and mathematicians and statisticians by 8 percent. That’s a lot higher than the total employment growth rate of just 3 percent over the decade.

Data analyst vs. data scientist: What’s the difference?

Data analysts and data scientists both work with data, but what they do with it differs. Data analysts typically work with existing data to solve defined business problems. Data scientists build new algorithms and models to make predictions about the future. Learn more about the difference between data scientists and data analysts.

Types of data analysts

As advancing technology has rapidly expanded the types and amount of information we can collect, knowing how to gather, sort, and analyze data has become a crucial part of almost any industry. You’ll find data analysts in the criminal justice, fashion, food, technology, business, environment, and public sectors—among many others.

People who perform data analysis might have other titles, such as:

Medical and health care analyst
Market research analyst
Business analyst
Business intelligence analyst
Operations research analyst
Intelligence analyst

Interested in business intelligence?

Gain the business and data skills you need for an entry-level business analyst role with IBM's Business Analyst Professional Certificate program. In as little as three months, you'll gain critical skills like business systems analysis, project risk management, and interactive data visualization.

How to become a data analyst

You can find data analytics jobs in all sorts of industries, and there’s more than one path toward securing your first job in this high-demand field. Whether you’re just getting started in the professional world or pivoting to a new career, here are some steps toward becoming a data analyst.

Get a foundational education.

If you’re new to the world of data analysis, you’ll want to start by developing some foundational knowledge in the field. Getting a broad overview of data analytics can help you decide whether this career is a good fit while equipping you with job-ready skills.

It used to be that most entry-level data analyst positions required a bachelor’s degree. While many positions still do require a degree, that’s beginning to change. You can develop foundational knowledge and enhance your resume with a degree in math, computer science, or another related field— or you can also learn what you need through alternative programs, like professional certificates, bootcamps, or self-study courses.

Resources to start your data analyst career

We've curated a collection of resources to help you decide whether becoming a data analyst is right for you—including figuring out what skills you'll need to learn and courses you can take to pursue this career.

Build your technical skills.

Getting a job in data analysis typically requires having a set of specific technical skills. Whether you’re learning through a degree program, professional certificate, or on your own, these are some essential skills you’ll likely need to get hired.

Statistics
R or Python programming
SQL (Structured Query Language)
Data visualization
Data cleaning and preparation

Take a look at some job listings for roles you’d like to apply for, and focus your learning on the specific programming languages or visualization tools listed as requirements.

In addition to these hard skills, hiring managers also look for workplace skills, like solid communication skills—you may be asked to present your findings to those without as much technical knowledge—problem-solving ability, and domain knowledge in the industry you’d like to work.

Learn more:
7 In-Demand Data Analyst Skills to Get Hired

Work on projects with real data.

The best way to learn how to find value in data is to work with it in real-world settings. Look for degree programs or courses that include hands-on projects using real data sets. You can also find a variety of free public data sets you can use to design your own projects.

Dig into climate data from the National Centers for Environmental Information, delve deeper into the news with data from BuzzFeed, or come up with solutions to looming challenges on Earth and beyond with NASA open data. These are just a few examples of the data out there. Pick a topic you’re interested in and find some data to practice on.

Read more:
5 Data Analytics Projects for Beginners

Develop a portfolio of your work.

As you play around with data sets on the internet or complete hands-on assignments in your classes, be sure to save your best work for your portfolio. A portfolio demonstrates your skills to hiring managers. A strong portfolio can go a long way toward getting the job.

As you start to curate work for your portfolio, choose projects that demonstrate your ability to:

Scrape data from different sources
Clean and normalize raw data
Visualize your findings through graphs, charts, maps, and other visualizations
Draw actionable insights from data

If you’ve worked on any group projects through the course of your learning, consider including one of those as well. This shows that you’re able to work as part of a team.

If you’re not sure what to include in your portfolio (or need some inspiration for project ideas), spend some time browsing through other people’s portfolios to see what they’ve chosen to include.

Read more:
How to Build a Data Analyst Portfolio: Tips for Success

Get an entry-level data analyst job.

After gaining some experience working with data and presenting your findings, it’s time to polish your resume and begin applying for entry-level data analyst jobs. Don’t be afraid to apply for positions that feel like a stretch. Your skills, portfolio, and enthusiasm for a role can often matter more than if you check every bullet item in the qualifications list.

If you’re still in school, ask your university’s career services office about any internship opportunities. With an internship, you can start gaining real-world experience for your resume and apply what you’re learning on the job.

There’s more than one path toward a career as a data analyst. Whether you've just graduated from school or are looking to switch careers, the first step is often assessing what transferable skills you have and building the new skills you’ll need in this new role.

Consider certification or an advanced degree.

As you move through your career as a data analyst, consider how you’d like to advance and what other qualifications can help you get there. Certifications, like the Certified Analytics Professional or Cloudera Certified Associate Data Analyst, may help qualify you for more advanced positions at higher pay grades.

If you’re considering advancing into a role as a data scientist, you may need to earn a master’s degree in data science or a related field. Advanced degrees are not always required, but having one can open up more opportunities.

Data analyst career advancement

Being a data analyst can also open doors to other careers. Many who start as data analysts go on to work as data scientists. Like analysts, data scientists use statistics, math, and computer science to analyze data. A scientist, however, might use advanced techniques to build models and other tools to provide insights into future trends.
